claims: Isso can resume prior discourse or a previously mentioned situation in Brazilian Portuguese.
Isto may be used cataphorically in more monitored/traditional descriptions, while actual Brazilian usage often broadens isso.

claims: Traditional descriptions distinguish este/isto from esse/isso by deictic relation.
In Brazilian Portuguese, esse/essa/isso commonly extend into contexts traditionally associated with este/esta/isto.

claims: Ninguém is an invariable indefinite pronoun and normally triggers singular verbal agreement.
Preverbal ninguém can license sentential negation without não; postverbal ninguém commonly occurs with preverbal não.
entries.notes: PASS R44: concordancia y negación correctamente explicadas; sin corrección material.

claims: Algo functions as an invariable indefinite pronoun referring to an unspecified thing, fact or content.
The contrast with alguém and nada is pedagogically accurate.

Preverbal nada may negate without não, while postverbal nada commonly co-occurs with preverbal não in Portuguese negative concord.
